prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1001; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but I'm happy to answer your questions about the accident.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the accident happened?
A: It was at an intersection in Pearland, Texas. I was turning left across traffic when another vehicle hit my car on the driver's side.
Q: What time of day was it, and what were the weather and road conditions?
A: It was in the afternoon. It was clear and dry. The road was normal, nothing unusual.
Q: Before you began your turn, what did you do?
A: I stopped at the line, looked both ways, and saw the oncoming car a good distance away. I thought I had time to make the turn, so I started moving.
Q: How fast were you going when the impact happened?
A: I was going slowly, maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour. I was almost through the turn when the other car came into my side.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle until the moment of impact?
A: Not clearly. It came up quickly, and I didn't have time to react.
Q: Were you hurt, and if so, what symptoms have you had?
A: Yes. My neck is stiff and sore, and I have pain in my lower back that gets worse when I sit for a long time. I was seen at a clinic and told I have a neck and back strain.
Q: Have you missed any work or daily activities because of these injuries?
A: I've had to cut back on lifting and driving for longer trips. I'm still working, but it's uncomfortable.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I did my best to avoid the collision, and I'm hoping this can be resolved so I can get back to normal.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
